schedule.name: Blackleg (Black Quarter)
schedule.desc: Clostridial soil-borne infection — sudden death in young cattle.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate annually before rainy season when bacterial spores activate.

schedule.name: Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD)
schedule.desc: Viral — skin nodules, fever, reduced milk production; spread by biting insects.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate before rainy/insect season.

schedule.name: Rift Valley Fever (RVF)
schedule.desc: Viral — outbreaks after flooding; zoonotic and fatal in calves/lambs.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate after flood events or before high-rainfall season.

schedule.name: Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD)
schedule.desc: Highly contagious viral disease — blisters on mouth/feet. Massive economic losses.
schedule.notes: SAT serotypes are Africa-specific. Vaccine must match circulating serotype.
schedule.vaccineType: Inactivated polyvalent (O, A, SAT1, SAT2, SAT3)

schedule.name: Anthrax
schedule.desc: Zoonotic bacterial disease — sudden death, spores persist in soil for decades.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate annually before rainy season. DO NOT open anthrax carcasses — burn/bury deep.

schedule.name: Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP)
schedule.desc: Bacterial lung disease — severe pneumonia, spread by close contact.
schedule.notes: AU-IBAR priority disease. Government campaigns common in endemic areas.

schedule.name: Rabies (Cattle)
schedule.desc: Important near wildlife reserves and high dog-population areas.

govInfo.service: Federal Dept of Veterinary & Pest Control Services (FDVPCS)
govInfo.note: NVRI Vom produces most vaccines domestically. Cold chain breaks in rural north. Private vets available in urban areas.

schedule.name: Goat Pox / Sheep Pox
schedule.desc: Viral — skin lesions, fever, respiratory signs; significant mortality in young animals.

schedule.name: Clostridial Diseases (Enterotoxemia, Tetanus)
schedule.desc: Enterotoxemia (overeating disease) and tetanus — sudden death especially in young animals.
schedule.notes: Booster 4 weeks before kidding/lambing to protect newborns via colostrum.

schedule.name: Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia (CCPP)
schedule.desc: Severe lung disease in goats — can reach 100% mortality in naive herds.

schedule.name: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR)
schedule.desc: A major small ruminant killer across Africa — 70–80% mortality in naive herds.
schedule.notes: FAO/WOAH global eradication campaign targeting 2030. Government campaigns very common.

schedule.name: Bluetongue (Sheep)
schedule.desc: Insect-borne viral disease — mainly affects sheep; facial swelling, lameness.
schedule.notes: South Africa vaccinates with trivalent formulations sequentially.

schedule.notes: Administered at hatchery. Reputable hatcheries include it in day-old chick price.

schedule.name: Gumboro Disease (IBD)
schedule.desc: Destroys the bursa of Fabricius in young chicks — severe immune suppression.

schedule.name: Newcastle Disease (ND)
schedule.desc: A major poultry killer across Africa — 90–100% mortality in unvaccinated village flocks.
schedule.notes: I-2 thermostable vaccine works without cold chain — ideal for African village conditions.
schedule.vaccineType: Live (HB1, La Sota, I-2 thermostable for village birds)

schedule.name: Fowl Typhoid (Salmonellosis)
schedule.desc: Salmonella Gallinarum — acute systemic disease; high mortality in young birds.

schedule.name: Avian Influenza (H5N1)
schedule.desc: Highly pathogenic AI — typically controlled by biosecurity and culling, NOT vaccination.
schedule.notes: Only Egypt routinely vaccinates poultry against AI in Africa. Other countries: strict biosecurity + mandatory culling.

schedule.name: Fowl Pox
schedule.desc: Viral — skin warts on comb/wattles; diphtheritic form in throat causes mortality.

govInfo.service: General Directorate of Animal Health & Production
govInfo.note: Sudan has one of Africa's largest livestock populations. RVF risk along Nile flood plains.

schedule.name: Rift Valley Fever (RVF)
schedule.desc: Viral — outbreaks after flooding; zoonotic and fatal in calves/lambs.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate after flood events or before high-rainfall season.

schedule.name: Blackleg (Black Quarter)
schedule.desc: Clostridial soil-borne infection — sudden death in young cattle.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate annually before rainy season when bacterial spores activate.

schedule.name: Brucellosis
schedule.desc: Causes abortion storms; zoonotic — undulant fever in humans from raw milk.
schedule.notes: ONLY vaccinate heifers (4–8 months). NEVER bulls or pregnant cows.
schedule.vaccineType: Live S19 (calves) / RB51 (adults) — heifers once in lifetime

schedule.name: Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD)
schedule.desc: Viral — skin nodules, fever, reduced milk production; spread by biting insects.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate before rainy/insect season.

schedule.name: Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD)
schedule.desc: Highly contagious viral disease — blisters on mouth/feet. Massive economic losses.
schedule.notes: SAT serotypes are Africa-specific. Vaccine must match circulating serotype.
schedule.vaccineType: Inactivated polyvalent (O, A, SAT1, SAT2, SAT3)

schedule.name: Anthrax
schedule.desc: Zoonotic bacterial disease — sudden death, spores persist in soil for decades.
schedule.notes: Vaccinate annually before rainy season. DO NOT open anthrax carcasses — burn/bury deep.

schedule.name: Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP)
schedule.desc: Bacterial lung disease — severe pneumonia, spread by close contact.
schedule.notes: AU-IBAR priority disease. Government campaigns common in endemic areas.

schedule.name: Rabies (Cattle)
schedule.desc: Important near wildlife reserves and high dog-population areas.

schedule.name: Goat Pox / Sheep Pox
schedule.desc: Viral — skin lesions, fever, respiratory signs; significant mortality in young animals.

schedule.name: Clostridial Diseases (Enterotoxemia, Tetanus)
schedule.desc: Enterotoxemia (overeating disease) and tetanus — sudden death especially in young animals.
schedule.notes: Booster 4 weeks before kidding/lambing to protect newborns via colostrum.

schedule.name: Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia (CCPP)
schedule.desc: Severe lung disease in goats — can reach 100% mortality in naive herds.

schedule.name: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR)
schedule.desc: A major small ruminant killer across Africa — 70–80% mortality in naive herds.
schedule.notes: FAO/WOAH global eradication campaign targeting 2030. Government campaigns very common.
